question: to the Commission Pascal Arimont (PPE), Joachim Streit (Renew), Thomas Pellerin-Carlin (S&D), Matej Tonin (PPE), Grégory Allione (Renew), Liesbet Sommen (PPE), Olivier Chastel (Renew), Vladimir Prebilič (Verts/ALE), Aurelijus Veryga (ECR), Christophe Clergeau (S&D) Subject:

The recently concluded European Citizens’ Panel on Preparedness brought together 150 randomly selected citizens from across all 27 Member States and resulted in 20 recommendations to strengthen the EU’s capacity to prevent and respond to crises. These recommendations address, among other issues, risk and crisis communication, warning systems, information integrity, inclusion, citizens’ self-sufficiency, volunteering and education on preparedness. In view of the Commission’s stated intention to incorporate these recommendations into the implementation of the Preparedness Union Strategy: 1.
Will the Commission publish a structured follow-up setting out which recommendations will be taken forward, by which services and within what time frame?
How does the Commission intend to follow up on recommendation 5.1 of the panel concerning volunteering and the strengthening of volunteer work?
How does the Commission assess the proposal to establish a European Preparedness Week as part of the follow-up to the citizens’ panel and the implementation of the Preparedness Union Strategy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) The Commission will publish a follow-up to the recommendations from the Citizens’ Panel on Preparedness in a Citizens’ Report. It will outline how it intends to respond to the recommendations, and in what time frame. The response will be prepared by the concerned Commission services. It is expected to be published before the Civil Protection Forum in November 2026. The Commission takes note of recommendation 5.1 (to strengthen volunteer work). The European Solidarity Corps offers cross-border volunteering activities and is identified as a key instrument for building a culture of preparedness. Through Action 30 of the Preparedness Union Strategy1, preparedness is now a formal priority within EU youth funding. The Commission is working on a set of guidelines for Member States on preparedness education for schools (Action 29), which could help to promote preparedness and volunteering (for example through activities with local organisations and emergency responders). The Commission is currently considering the rest of the suggestions proposed in the recommendations and will provide a response in the Citizens’ Report. The Commission welcomed the citizens’ recommendations on the European Preparedness Week, which aligns very well with the spirit of the Preparedness Union Strategy (in particular Action 27). In this context, the EU will propose an annual EU Preparedness Day to raise awareness on the topic. This is expected to be announced at the Civil Protection Forum (34 November 2026), with the first edition being held in 2027, at a date to be confirmed.
